title: Cheapest European countries for Nigerian students
summary: The file starts on her first word (0.15 s) and ends on "…I hope that it works out." with 0.25 s to spare, so there is no dead air to trim. She speaks in long run-on stretches with few real pauses; the cuts are 4 stumbles/retakes, 1 placeholder line and 1 long pause. Whisper heard "proof of funds" as "approval funds" all through and "work" as "walk": fixed in the transcripts.

cuts.why: "these official studies, official sources rather": keeps "go to these official sources rather".

"…situations where you pay like this and this and this. There are some new universities like this." She points at examples she never names. Cut keeps "…some situations where you pay. Now the major thing for a German student visa…"; the examples (Baden-Württemberg €1,500/semester, TUM) go on screen as in the kit.
"you have to check the university before you are," then again "you have to check the university that you're applying to". Keeps the full second take.

"for a study research, for the, for the proof of fund, the proof of, you know, living, as I think we call it proof of funds, we always call it proof of funds". Keeps "the Italian consulates list the minimum, so for the proof of funds is 10,179.85 euros a year".

decisions:
- **Cut 2 (2:17, the "like this and this and this" placeholder)**: if she prefers to keep it, the on-screen card has to carry the examples at exactly that moment.
- **11:51 "They're just, oh yeah, you see, the numbers from someone that is observing, I am just observing, I'm just clicking links and checking"**: loose but honest; an optional cut 711.97 to 715.95 would leave "They're just starting numbers. I'm just clicking links and checking." (not counted).
- **0:00-0:16 opening** is a little tangled ("someone has probably told you that Germany is free, and for tuition at most public universities, it is, but you also have the old proof of funds…"). It works, but the two pauses of 0.8 s in it could be tightened to 0.4 s.
- Unclear words to listen to: 9:55 "I have friends in my school that are paying (?) … so your program determines your fee" (whisper: "paying wheelers like to total vote on paying").
kit:
**Skipped from the kit:**
- France exemption caps (30% in 2026/27, 25% in 2027/28, 20% from 2028) were on-screen only; she says the decree "limits how many students each university can exempt". Fine.
- Italy: the University of Padua example (2027/28 applications opened 15 September 2026, first window closes 15 November 2026); she just says "the applications opened quite early".
- Austria: "A lot of people who would apply for a master's are probably 24 or older" and the "wait till you see what Austria does when you turn 24" tease.
- Norway: "UDI, Norway's immigration office" by name.
- Kit line "Germany is also planning to raise its student support rate in 2027 … check it again before you open your blocked account": said, but she trails off ("check it again before you like, you know, decide").

**Added in the recording:** the opening disclaimer ("please, this is a disclaimer… go to these official sources"); "I work full time alongside my master's so I'm talking from experience"; "Maybe I'll do a video on scholarships separately" (she has one: scholarships-for-african-students-in-europe); "I did reasonably research but I didn't go in depth"; Paris rent "is gonna choke you".

**Facts to check (what she says vs the kit):**
- 3:02 Germany work rule: she says "140 full days or 280 days" (whisper heard "144"); the rule is 140 full days or 280 half days. She drops "half": a caption should say half days.
- 4:04 France proof of funds: she says "about 10,000 plus euros a year"; kit has about €10,530. Fine.
- 5:01 **France work limit: she says "nearly 60 hours a year"**; the kit (and the rule) is **964 hours a year**. Needs a caption fix or a cut.
- 6:44 Austria: "plus a small student union fee, also get about like one five(?) euros in a year": kit says altogether about €1,506 a year (€726.72 x 2 + €26.20). Unclear in the audio.
- 7:08 Austria's no-fee country list: she names Benin, Ethiopia, Senegal(?), Togo, Uganda (whisper garbled the first three); kit has the same five.
- 7:31 Austria under 24: "about 8k plus" (kit €8,671); 24+: "about 15,700" ✓.
- 8:15 Czech: 115,810 Czech crowns "about 6,000 US dollars" (the embassy page's own figure per the kit; kit's card shows about €4,750).
- 9:03 Tallinn University: she says most master's cost "between 4,000-5,000 euros a year"; kit says 4,000 to 5,200. Her own programme: "I'm paying 6,000 … increased to 7k" ✓ (kit: €7,000 for new non-EU students).
- 10:09 Norway charging tuition "from 2023 I think": kit says from autumn 2023 ✓. NHH 204,000 kroner ✓, UDI about 170,000 kroner ✓ (kit: NOK 170,368).
- 10:36 Finland UEF €10,000-12,000, Migri €9,600 ✓.
- 11:32 Summary: "If you're under 24, Austria is one of the cheapest" (whisper: "on the trend of fall") ✓ kit.
